small_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose3d now dominates (fused post-kernel is tiny vs 18.6ms total, baseline 6ms). Tuning BLOCK_C/BLOCK_PW/num_warps of the post kernel cannot recover the gap; only minor wins remain there.
- If staying small, fold the bias of conv_transpose into the post-kernel and try `channels_last_3d` memory format on the conv input to speed cuDNN, plus `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True`.
- Increase BLOCK_PW to 16 and try num_warps=2 since the post-kernel is memory-bound and tiny.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) that computes the `input × weight` outer product and scatter-adds into the output grid honoring stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1. This is the heavy op (~12ms of the 18.6ms) and the only path to fast_p > 1.
- Alternatively, implement as a gather-style direct conv: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile); for each output voxel, gather the contributing input voxels via the transposed-conv index formula `(o + pad - k) / stride` with divisibility mask. This avoids atomics entirely and lets you fuse bias + the entire post-pipeline (maxpool, softmax, sub, swish, channel-max) in one persistent epilogue when the output tile aligns to the pool window.
- Fuse conv_transpose epilogue (bias add) with the existing pool/softmax/sub/swish/max kernel by producing tile-sized conv output blocks aligned to the pool window, eliminating the full conv-output write/read round trip (~33M elements at fp32).
